question.knowledge_point: Finding the Velocity of a Particle Whose Acceleration Is Given By a Polynomial
question.problem: A particle moves along a straight line relative to a fixed origin $O$ with acceleration, measured in $\text{m}/{\text{s}}^{2},$ given by the function $a(t)=2-3{t}^{2}$, where $t$ is the time in seconds. If the particle has velocity $v=4\,\text{m}/\text{s}$ when $t=1\,\text{s}$, find the velocity (in $\text{m/s}$) of the particle at time $t.$
question.worked_solution:
First, we find $v(t)$ by integrating the acceleration with respect to time:

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =\int a(t)\text{d}t \\  & =\int (2-3{t}^{2})\text{d}t \\  & =2t-{t}^{3}+C\end{aligned}
$$

To determine $C$, we use the fact that $v(1)=4.$ Substituting this into the above gives

$$
\begin{aligned}4 & =2(1)-(1)^{3}+C \\ 4 & =2-1+C \\ C & =3.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the velocity $v$ of the particle at time $t$ is $v(t)=3+2t-{t}^{3}.$

evidence.solution_quote: Finally, the velocity $v$ of the particle at time $t$ is $v(t)=3+2t-{t}^{3}.$
